newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn denies it plans to sell Bundesbank gold.
newsitem.headline: Bonn denies it plans to sell Bundesbank gold.

text.p: A German Finance Ministry spokeswoman, denying a report by the weekly news magazine Stern, said on Tuesday Germany has no plans to sell gold from the Bundesbank's reserves.
"There are no plans to sell gold," the ministry spokeswoman said.

The magazine said some members of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition wanted to sell surplus gold starting in July 1998, after the startup of the European Central Bank made the Bundesbank reserves superfluous.
Bonn denies it plans to sell Bundesbank gold

Ministry spokeswoman Barbara Eckrich said no one would know how much of the European Central Bank's capital Germany would be called upon to supply until the number of participants in European monetary union had been determined.

Stern said the Bundesbank's share of the ECB's capital would be far less than the market value of its own reserves, and that some members of the coalition wanted to sell the excess gold to pay down Germany's debt.
